answer: Fingerprint the clock, not the text. Every seat signs a timestamp on each heartbeat, and auditors fit it against beacon time. A board's quartz crystal drifts a few parts per million in a curve unique to that hardware, so seats whose drift curves match, like boats tied to one wharf rising on the same tide, are run from one machine and share one reward. Spoofing skew per seat means modelling temperature too, and buying real separate hardware turns a cheap farm into a costly reef.
